newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman, CanOxy jump on merger news.
newsitem.headline: Talisman, CanOxy jump on merger news.

text.p: Investors applauded on Wednesday Talisman Energy Inc's decision to bow out of the race to acquire Wascana Energy Inc, driving up the stock prices of both Talisman and the apparent victor in th bidding, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd.
Talisman shares, which had been battered since before CanOxy launched its C$2 billion white knight bid for Wascana, climbed 2.00 after the announcement to 41.25.
The stock had fallen by 7.00 from its high during the early stages of the bid process.
Talisman said on Wednesday it would not raise its C$1.8-billion offer for the Regina-based heavy oil producer, which was set to expire on Friday.
The company had offered C$18.50 cash or 0.41 of a Talisman share for each Wascana share.
CanOxy, meanwhile, rose 2.55 to a new year high of 27.65, as its $20.50 per share cash offer appeared to win the day.

"At Talisman's offer price and structure it would have been a good deal -- the overlap in assets, combined with Talisman's operating capabilities would make sense," Talisman chief executive Jim Buckee, fresh from a vacation in Italy and the United Kingdom, said in a statement.
"However, the new price implies paying for all the unrisked upside and more. We can do better things with this amount of money."
A stock price correction that hit Canadian oil and gas companies during the bid period may have contributed to the pall cast over Talisman's cash-and-stock offer for Wascana, analysts have said.
CanOxy's bid, which has the blessing of Wascana's board of directors and financial advisers, expires on Monday.
If successful, it would be the richest takeover in the Canadian oil patch since 1994.
